question: What has happened to the Great Lakes vowel shift, the Northern Cities Shift, among speakers born since the 1980s?
answer: It is retreating in several cities. Older speakers in Michigan and upstate New York say cot close to cat and cat almost as kyat; a Lansing study of speakers born across the 20th century found the youngest backing away from both, though one part carried on. Grandparents and grandchildren now split on cat.
move: A trend that ran for decades can reverse within a single generation.
ask: What trend I think will keep going could reverse within one generation?
source: Wagner et al., Penn Working Papers, 2016
reference: Wagner, Mason, Nesbitt, Pevan & Savage, Reversal and Re-Organization of the Northern Cities Shift in Michigan, University of Pennsylvania Working Papers in Linguistics 22(2), 2016
